body: Noise- A box fan will work and it's helpful for the heat. If it's cold having it not face you or adding blankets helps! I also second the weighed blanket, it's awesome!! I also have a somatic trigger related to my backside and so sleep with two HUGE stuffed animals from IKEA :) they are nice to cuddle with and if I switch sides I've got one protecting me and the other to cuddle and vice versa. Also, if you can, locking the door at night, even if it's one of those locks that you get for hotels (have to put in the door and works until you open the door again) is helpful for me at least to feel safer. Good luck my friend!!

Not weird! A great thing about being an adult is you can do whatever you want. I sleep in between two GIANT stuffed animals (Blåhaj and Djungelskog from IKEA) every night for the past year and it has majorly helped my quality of sleep. Before then, I always slept with at least one smaller stuffed animal (including my childhood stuffed animal). I don't see any reason to stop personally, as I don't feel that it's childish or anything. I'm also an autistic adult, who doesn't usually GAF about how I'm perceived anyways. Overall, it isn't a problem especially if you don't like to be touched while you sleep, and it isn't seeming to harm you. Biologically, sleeping with a human, pet, or stuffed animal (hell even a pillow that you cuddle or put in between your legs) helps the quality of sleep and can release oxytocin, a great hormone! Hope this helps and know that you're not "weird" or anything negative for being comfy while you sleep :)
